blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: After a team adds a tool, some conversations fail with a 400 or lose the model's reasoning when they are resumed from the database. The save code keeps only the text of each reply. What is the best fix?

options.text: Save the usage totals with each turn so that the conversation can be rebuilt from them
options.says: Ruled out because usage totals are "cost, and an early warning for the context window", not a way to rebuild a conversation.

options.text: Store each reply's content list exactly as received and send it back unchanged
options.says: Storing only text drops `tool_use` and thinking blocks, and the page says to "store the content list as received".

options.text: Save the model id with each turn so that the same tier answers after a resume
options.says: Ruled out because the model id belongs to the "settings that do not change per turn", and it does not carry blocks.

options.text: Follow every tool result with an explanatory text block when the turn is rebuilt
options.says: Ruled out because adding text after tool results "can teach the model to expect user input after every tool call".

questions.stem: A client receives `stop_reason` of `max_tokens` on the fifth turn of a conversation. Which handling fits the module?

options.text: Mark the reply truncated, keep it in the history, and let the user ask to continue next
options.says: A truncated reply is kept: "cut replies stay in the history", and the user can ask to continue in a normal turn.

options.text: End the list with the cut text as an assistant turn so that the model resumes writing
options.says: Ruled out because "a request that does returns a 400 invalid_request_error", and ending the list with an assistant turn is a prefill.

options.text: Treat the turn as failed and remove it, because a cut reply is not a whole exchange
options.says: Ruled out because the rollback rule is to "commit a turn only when the whole exchange succeeded", and a cut reply is a completed exchange.

options.text: Raise the sampling temperature so that the model finishes inside the limit the next time it runs
options.says: Ruled out because "a non-default value of any of them is rejected with a 400 error", and sampling does not control where the limit cuts.

origin.section: Cut replies stay in the history

questions.stem: A team wants an early warning before long chats approach the context window and become expensive. Which signal can the client compute from every reply?

options.text: The total of the three input-token fields in the usage object
options.says: The page says the total input is the sum of three numbers, and that counting tokens makes the growth visible.

options.text: The count of turns so far, since each turn adds the same number of tokens
options.says: Ruled out because "turn n sends about 200 n input tokens", so each turn adds more than the one before and a turn count is a poor proxy.

options.text: The output-token count alone, because the reply is what fills the window
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "the input cost of a conversation grows with the square of its length", and the history is input.

options.text: The appearance of the context-window stop reason, which says the limit is close
options.says: Ruled out because that value reports that "the context window filled before max_tokens", which is already too late.

origin.section: The cost of a long conversation

questions.stem: A developer logs each request body for debugging and finds that bodies logged earlier in a conversation change after later turns. Which defect fits best?

options.text: A failed call was not rolled back before the error finally left the function that made it
options.says: Ruled out because the rollback rule is to "commit a turn only when the whole exchange succeeded", and it concerns failures.

options.text: The assistant content was rebuilt from text and not stored as received
options.says: Ruled out because the page says to "store the content list as received", which concerns what a turn contains, not whether old requests change.

options.text: The payload holds the client's own history list instead of a snapshot of it
options.says: The page describes it: "if the request body holds the client's own history list, a later turn changes earlier requests".

options.text: The system prompt is resent with every turn and grows each time
options.says: Ruled out because "system is the same top-level field on every request", so it does not grow.
